{"regions":[{"label":"Table 6.2 — Recommendations organized according to a maturity model based on data safeguards and enablers","kind":"table","bbox":[0.094,0.088,0.916,0.659],"summary":"Three-stage maturity model table comparing recommended safeguards and enablers for a country’s data system: establishing fundamentals, initiating data flows, and optimizing the system.","details":"The table has three columns: “Stage of country’s data system,” “Safeguards,” and “Enablers.” Rows and content:

• Establishing fundamentals. Safeguards: Conduct a baseline needs assessment. Develop a comprehensive policy framework based on best practices that (1) safeguards personal, nonpersonal, and evolving categories of data and promotes greater equity around data; (2) enhances the security of systems and infrastructure that protect against misuse of data; (3) expands individuals’ agency and control over their personal data; and (4) promotes certainty and predictability, integrating fundamental safeguards discussed in the chapter, such as data protection and cybersecurity. Enablers: Conduct a baseline needs assessment. Develop a comprehensive policy framework based on best practices that enables the use and sharing of data for development purposes, ensuring access, openness, interoperability, portability, predictability, and transparency, while integrating fundamental enablers discussed in the chapter, such as electronic transactions.

• Initiating data flows. Safeguards: Elaborate a legal framework embodying policy prerogatives that include personal data protection; promotion of cybersecurity and combating cybercrime; regulation of competition; and provisions for establishing relevant enforcement institutions. Enablers: Elaborate a legal framework embodying policy prerogatives that include legal recognition of e-transactions; access to information; intellectual property rights for nonpersonal data; openness of public intent data, including use of licenses that encourage data sharing; and data classification principles.

• Optimizing the system. Safeguards: Promote awareness of safeguards domestically through adoption of data protection by design and default, together with associated cybersecurity measures; internationally through cross-border interoperability of data protection standards; address more complex issues such as mixed data and group rights; ensure sufficient capacity of institutions responsible for oversight; and establish metrics to monitor and evaluate implementation and enforcement of these policies and laws. Enablers: Consider issues such as data portability and increasing incentives around sharing private intent data; ensure sufficient capacity of institutions responsible for oversight; and establish metrics to monitor and evaluate implementation of these policies, laws, and institutions.

Source: WDR 2021 team. No numeric units or values; the table is qualitative.","limitations":"Text and table structure are legible. No material ambiguity detected."}]}
